name: Linux
title: A straightforward VPN for Linux.
lead: Traverse's Linux page highlights graphical and command-line options for users who want privacy without a complicated setup.
description: Connect your Linux computer through an encrypted VPN tunnel, choose a server location, and keep the same everyday privacy tools close at hand. The original product page describes support for popular distributions and both GUI and CLI workflows.
imageAlt: Laptop open and ready for work in a café

highlights.title: GUI and CLI options
highlights.text: Choose the workflow that fits your setup, whether you prefer a graphical app or terminal controls.

highlights.title: Common distributions
highlights.text: The original Linux page names Ubuntu, Debian, Fedora, Linux Mint, and Arch among its supported options.

highlights.title: Open standards
highlights.text: Traverse describes support for established VPN protocols such as WireGuard and OpenVPN.

steps.title: Choose your plan

steps.title: Install for your distro
steps.text: Follow the current Linux download instructions for your distribution and architecture.

steps.title: Connect your way
steps.text: Use the app or the documented command-line workflow to connect to a server.

detailsTitle: Privacy with room for your workflow

details.title: Encrypted connection
details.text: Route traffic through the VPN to add privacy on networks you do not control.

details.title: Leak safeguards
